messages:
Amal: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection change we see a /5-10% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for chat workloads vs baseline. patterns look workload-specific.
Kevin: saw that in infra alerts, perf-bot triggered the regression alert at 11:02. id: kswap-17485.
perf-bot: [alert] prefix_cache_hitrate drop > 4% (prod-edge-west) — rollback window open for 30m.
Sophia: interesting — is this across all seq lengths or concentrated? any delta between RAG vs pure completion?
Amal: concentrated on short-prefix chat flows (turns < 80 tokens) and structured-output prompts that include JSON schema. RAG with long docs actually unchanged or slightly better.
Kevin: dug into traces. when kernel switched to tiled-gemm-optim, we changed micro-batching behavior (coalescing threshold moved). That increased the effective key split frequency for short prefixes -> fewer prefix matches.
Rachel: can you paste a sample trace? even a minimal flamegraph snippet helps.
Kevin: pasting short capture from our microbench:
```
# perf capture (trace-id: kswap-17485)
prefetch_score: 0.42 -> 0.18
kcache_hits: 1482/3720 (39.8%) <- baseline ~45.3%
batch_coalesce(ms): 1.2 -> 3.8
kernel: tiled-gemm-optim v2
decision: merge_when_tokens>32 changed to >64
```
Sophia: aha — coalesce increase means requests arriving in slightly different alignment get different prefix keys due to sequence padding + kv-shard boundaries. makes sense.
Amal: hypothesis: our cache key uses (model, token_len_bucket, prefix_hash, kernel_variant). kernel_variant flip breaks matches unless we normalize key to canonical model+prefix only.
Kevin: we tried key normalization in staging (strip kernel_variant) — hit-rate recovered but latency SLOs worsened on long RAG because kernel picks were suboptimal for long sequences. tradeoff.
Rachel: so need workload-aware keying. maybe include kernel hints only for buckets where kernel selection materially changes output (long context path) else ignore.
Sophia: propose warmup strategy: for chat flows, do quick ephemeral prefetch of top-k next-prefixes using convo-turn bucketing right after session open. for RAG, prefer persistent KV with longer TTL and sequence-bucketing by doc-chunk-id.
Amal: agree. also let's add a metric: prefix_affinity = hits / (hits + near_miss_count) to capture key stability. add to dashboards.
Kevin: I added a quick panel on perf dashboard: /dash/prefix-affinity?trace=kswap-17485 (link internal). current affinity: chat 0.61 -> baseline 0.72. RAG 0.85 unchanged.
Rachel: next actions: 1) ramp rollback of kernel change on edge-west for 2h to confirm causality (canary already queued), 2) experiment with key normalization toggle + kernel-hint gating, 3) implement chat ephemeral prefetch prototype.
Amal: assigning: @Kevin to run rollback canary and collect cold/hot traces; @Sophia to prototype ephemeral prefetch (3 days), @Rachel to own dashboard + runbook update. I'll coordinate with infra to extend canary window if needed.
Kevin: started rollback canary + will attach microbench results: `./perf/run_prefetch_bench --scenario chat-ephemeral --runs 100`.
Sophia: initial prototype suggestion: prefix prefetch uses convo-turn hash + last-3-tokens fingerprint, TTL 12s, max prefetch 4. keep it cheap.
Rachel: noted for runbook: include detection heuristic (prefix_affinity drop > 5% and simultaneous kernel_variant flips) -> auto-alert + suggested mitigations.
Amal: thanks team. keep updates here; if we confirm kernel is root cause we'll coordinate a tuned kernel release instead of blanket rollback.
Kevin: update in 20m with canary numbers.
perf-bot: [info] canary roll started by Kevin at 1748503445 (canary id=c-17485-1).
